# Content review — 14 September 2026

Scope: all 15 chapters, eight downloadable prompts, nine original Mermaid flows, and the source ledger. This is a review of the book; Signal Garden and its video pipeline remain proposed projects.

## Method and evidence

Read the source passages supporting technical and research claims, compared the claims with the linked documentation, and checked the manuscript for conflicting rules and incomplete command sequences. Preferred primary material published or updated since 1 March 2026. Kept undated live documentation and explicitly labeled older background. A review date is not a publication date.

The book now maps every chapter introduction and subsection to a source check record. Records distinguish documented behavior, research findings, synthesis, original proposals, and retrieval limitations. Each source provides main-item summaries, a passage locator, review date, and limitations. The data lives in `book/evidence.json` and `book/sources.json`; the rendered book links directly to the resources and reading notes.

## Corrections

- Git setup: stage the complete new scaffold, including entry/configuration/assets; inspect actual staged content. Preserve unrelated changes in existing projects. Document GitHub CLI prerequisites.
- PR example: keep the fixed-camera design and create the description file before `--body-file` reads it.
- Game rules: restart from paused, won, or lost resets the complete round and enters playing. Focus loss pauses and clears input; returning requires explicit Resume. Align the brief, bootstrap prompt, review skill, and acceptance table.
- Milestones: M2 is a playable win slice. M3 still supplies both loss conditions and drone/health pressure.
- Skills: automatic invocation depends on eligibility and configuration; a catalog budget may shorten or omit entries. None of the cited independent benchmarks tests Astra game development.
- Godot: the HTML entry may be named index.html; retain the other export filenames. The documented PWA isolation workaround prevents an overbroad claim that threaded Pages exports are always impossible.
- Browser behavior: cite animation timing, background pause, audio autoplay, and reduced motion. A callback interval is not GPU render duration; performance targets remain proposals.
- Video jobs: include THROTTLED, retryable status-request errors, uncertain submissions, unknown states, and bounded waits. A local timeout does not cancel the remote job.
- Video assets: Comfy get_output returns download instructions, not a saved local file. Cloud model/template availability requires its own check.
- Trailer fidelity: the Runway multi-shot recipe generates shots; the mixed-source storyboard needs real captured gameplay composed separately.
- Thinking flows: add explicit outcomes for exhausted effort or blocked progress.
- Source metadata: update Spec Kit and GDQuest dates, correct the book’s dependency description, and add ten official references for previously uncited technical behavior.

## Retrieval limits

Source 02’s selected keynote passage was checked through its transcript mirror. Source 03’s Pickscribe mirror timed out; an alternative exposed a landing page without transcript text. The prior speech summary was withdrawn from verified evidence, and the original video remains only a historical reading lead. Current context advice is supported independently by source 17.

The Remotion companion video and GDQuest associated video have no transcript evidence in this edition. Their accessible written guides support the corresponding instructions. No invented timecodes, claims of watching unavailable video, or new paid video jobs are included.

The expanded edition has 54 ledger entries with checked content and one explicitly limited historical video lead. This includes the earlier review's checks, not a claim that every source was independently re-fetched in the latest pass. Original game rules, prompts, rubrics, comparison procedures, and diagrams require practical evaluation in the intended project.

## Expanded logic and STEM review

Read all 16 English chapter files and the embedded game prompts. Cross-checked
the new material in the Vietnamese and Korean editions. This pass revisited
current Astra prompting/skill guidance, the Astra game case study, skill
discovery documentation, the three research preprints, the SkillsBench
leaderboard, Godot export constraints, and Runway output expiry. It added
seven directly read primary references, numbered 49-55. Publication dates
were not invented for undated repositories.

Concrete corrections and additions:

- Distinguish game versions V1/V2 from prompt versions P1/P2. Existing code,
  improved briefs, added tools, and human interventions confound a wording-only
  comparison. The example P3 is a repair-stage prompt, not a superior bootstrap.
- Preserve prompts together with outcomes. Distill verified lessons; route
  them to the brief, regression checks, conventions, or a justified procedure.
  Compare candidates from the same revision and evaluate held-out scenarios.
- State that prompt revision changes supplied instructions, not model weights.
  Six versus eight successes out of ten is +20 percentage points, about +33%
  relative, and insufficient by itself to establish general superiority.
- Make keyboard normalization explicit, including zero input and seconds-based
  units. Keep analog-stick magnitude distinct from digital normalization.
  Elapsed-time scaling alone does not prevent collision tunneling.
- Define activation range as inclusive ground-plane centre-to-centre distance
  of 2 units. Damage/time updates precede loss resolution and activation.
- Clarify that rAF intervals are callback cadence, not proof of frame
  presentation or GPU execution duration. Specify the percentile estimator.
- Choose Godot's index.html at export time; do not rename generated output.
- Inspect GitHub candidates by purpose and dependency structure: OpenAI's
  web-game-foundations, Remotion's maintained collection, a community creative
  director, and Comfy's current cloud package. No skills were installed into
  the agent's active catalog or benchmarked for this book.
- Identify the mandatory interview in the community director as a possible
  mismatch for a complete brief. Preserve shared references outside SKILL.md.
- Comfy's current README marks the legacy skills folder frozen; its canonical
  cloud plugin targets Claude Code and comfy-cli bundles its own separate skills.
- SkillAlchemy Table 5 juxtaposes PDF-redaction instruction labels and a
  threejs-to-obj reuse description. Retain the reported main findings with
  their model/task limits, but do not rely on that table as clean transfer
  evidence or silently resolve the inconsistency in the author's favor.
- OpenAI's dataset-backed optimizer notice schedules legacy Evals read-only
  access for 31 October 2026 and shutdown for 30 November 2026. The proposed
  local comparison does not depend on that retiring hosted product.
- Correct the generated establishing-shot example to the brief's teal beacon.

## Illustration and export provenance

Actually rendered two original stills using Blender 4.5.3 LTS from the sibling
3d_astra tool installation at the user's request. The procedural script and
editable .blend scene are included. Camera, geometry, and lighting match;
object materials change. The images use neutral study lighting, not a claim
that the proposed dusk game is complete. A newer portable Blender was used
for an initial draft before the user directed reuse of the sibling tool;
the published renders were rebuilt with that shared executable.

Mermaid CLI 11.17.0 exports the ten existing/new diagram definitions for PDFs;
the site uses its locked Mermaid 11.17.2 runtime. The diagrams describe
observable decisions, not private model reasoning. Neither renders nor graphs
implement Signal Garden or validate gameplay.

Three complete PDF editions are generated from the built HTML with embedded
font subsets, clickable links, contents, and bookmarks. Export checks cover
chapter presence and annotation links; rendered-page visual inspection is
separate. The PDF manifest records page counts and checksums. CI verifies
that the PDFs match the manuscript fingerprint and deployed copies.

## Website validation

The repository’s automated checks validate section/source coverage, stable IDs, source metadata, local links, downloadable prompts, and Mermaid source integrity. Real browser inspection is separate from these checks. Deployment success and public artifact verification belong to the release record; source-content verification does not substitute for either.

The earlier release passed its checks with 90 introductions/subsections covered, 48 source records, eight prompt downloads, and nine diagram definitions. Its local production preview rendered all nine diagrams without console errors.

The expanded release passed `npm run build` and `npm run check`: 96 covered introductions/subsections, 55 source records, eight prompt templates per language, ten diagram definitions per language, and matching full-book PDF checksums. English has 105 PDF pages, Vietnamese 103, and Korean 100. All pages were rendered for layout inspection; missing Vietnamese heading glyphs, Korean running-header glyphs, and a mathematical minus glyph were corrected. Chapter presence, missing-character extraction, and internal/external link annotations were checked. Longer diagrams use A3 foldout pages.

The local browser rendered all ten diagrams without console errors. The Blender figure pair, language-specific PDF links, light/dark styling, and Korean/Vietnamese mobile layout were inspected. The 390-pixel responsive viewport had no page-wide horizontal overflow. Temporary viewport settings were reset after inspection.
